title: Project Osprey kickoff
transcript:
Elena Vasquez: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for making the time. This is the formal kickoff for Project Osprey. Agenda is scope and timeline, team roles, the four workstreams, wall-crossing and information controls, and then action items with owners. We have about fifty minutes.
Hannah Swanson: Quick context for Erik and Susan, since you're newer to this one. It's a sell-side mandate. The client is looking at a full sale of a mid-market business services company. We're targeting a launch to buyers in early November, so the calendar is tight.
Elena Vasquez: Right. Working backward from a November 2 launch, I want a draft teaser and process letter by October 9, a first-pass buyer universe by October 12, and valuation model v1 by October 14. The CIM draft is due October 23. Tom, does that feel realistic?
Tom Hargreave: The CIM date is doable if we get the management financials by next week. The last data pull had gaps in the quarterly segment breakdown, so I'd like to push for a clean set by October 6. If it slips past that, the CIM draft slips with it.
Robert Price: I'll own the request to the client's finance team. I'll send the consolidated information request list today and ask for the segment data first, then the add-backs schedule.
Joshua Morales: On the add-backs, I'd flag that the quality of earnings view will drive how buyers read the adjusted EBITDA. We should have a position on the run-rate adjustments before the model goes out. Otherwise we'll rebuild it after the first buyer call.
Elena Vasquez: Agreed. Joshua, you're the day-to-day lead on the model and the QoE bridge. Susan, you'll support him on comps and precedent transactions.
Susan Harrington: Sounds good. For precedents I'm planning to screen the last five years of deals in the sector, with a size band of roughly one hundred to five hundred million of enterprise value. Is that the right band, or should I go wider?
Hannah Swanson: Start with that band, but include a separate tab for larger strategic deals. Strategics may pay up for synergies, and we want to show that range, not just the sponsor-style multiples.
Susan Harrington: Got it. Two tabs, one for the core band and one for large strategics.
Elena Vasquez: Next, the buyer universe. Hannah, this is yours with Erik.
Hannah Swanson: Yes. The plan is tiering. Tier one is strategic acquirers with obvious adjacency, tier two is sponsors with existing platforms in the space, and tier three is opportunistic or financial buyers. Erik, I'd like you to build the first-pass list with rationale for each name and a note on any known conflicts.
Erik Flores: Will do. Should I pull in our internal coverage notes, or keep it to public sources for the first pass?
Hannah Swanson: Public sources and our CRM relationship history only. Check with compliance before using anything else. We'll review the draft list together on October 12.
Tom Hargreave: One item on materials. I want a single owner for the CIM narrative so we don't end up with three voices. I can take that. Erik, you'll draft the industry overview section, and Susan, the financial summary pages once Joshua's model is stable.
Elena Vasquez: Fine. Tom owns the CIM. Now the controls piece, which is important. Osprey is wall-crossed only. The deal channel stays private, and nobody outside this group gets added without clearing it first. Please do not discuss the project in public channels or by name outside this team.
Robert Price: I'll confirm with Marcus Bell's team that our restricted list entry and the wall-crossing log are current. I'll also set up the data room structure in DocVault with access limited to this team, and we'll tie permissions to single sign-on groups.
Joshua Morales: Can we also agree on a code name convention for the buyers in drafts? Using real names in working files that get forwarded around makes me nervous.
Elena Vasquez: Good call. Use letter codes for buyers in all working drafts and keep the key in one restricted file. Erik, you maintain the key, and you hold it to the same access list as the data room.
Erik Flores: Understood. I'll set that up this afternoon.
Hannah Swanson: One risk to flag. If the client's auditors are late with the stub period review, we may not have clean numbers for launch. Should we plan a fallback of launching with unaudited interim figures clearly labeled?
Elena Vasquez: Let's keep it as a contingency, not the plan. Robert, please ask the client's CFO for the auditors' timetable in the same request. If it looks late, we decide at the October 14 checkpoint.
Robert Price: Noted, I'll include that.
Tom Hargreave: On cadence, can we do a short standup Monday, Wednesday and Friday at nine thirty, and a longer working session Thursdays?
Elena Vasquez: Yes. Standups are fifteen minutes, with status against the workplan only. Thursday sessions are for reviews, starting with the buyer list on the twelfth and the model on the fourteenth. Hannah, please keep the workplan tracker updated.
Hannah Swanson: Will do. I'll circulate it by end of day.
Elena Vasquez: Let me recap the action items. Robert sends the information request list today, chases segment data by October 6, and sets up the restricted data room and confirms the wall-crossing log with compliance. Joshua and Susan deliver model v1 by October 14, with Susan's two comps tabs ready by October 9. Erik builds the tiered buyer list by October 12 and sets up the buyer code key today. Tom drafts the teaser and process letter by October 9 and owns the CIM draft due October 23. Hannah owns the workplan tracker and the buyer list review. Anything missing?
Joshua Morales: I think that covers it. I'll send the QoE bridge outline to Tom by Monday so the CIM can reference it.
Elena Vasquez: Good, add that. Thanks, everyone. Let's get moving.
